status_summary: OSMRE published a final rule on 2026-02-19 (91 FR 7835, FR Doc. 2026-03301), effective 2026-03-23, rescinding its April 2024 ten-day notice rule and returning largely to the 2020 rule, with minor changes that streamline coordination with state regulators and recognize states as primary regulators on non-federal, non-Indian lands. The rule and the agency's release tie the change to Secretary's Order 3418. No action was found on moving the headquarters to Pittsburgh, cutting inspectors, the training program or the violator database.

timeline.event: OSMRE announced the final rule, describing it as prioritizing state leadership.
OSMRE published a final rule rescinding the 2024 ten-day notice rule and restoring the 2020 framework; effective 2026-03-23.

title: Keep state-led ten-day notice process at the Office of Surface Mining
uncertainties: A Federal Register API search of OSMRE rules and proposed rules since 2025-01-20 found none on the Applicant Violator System, training access or Directive INE-26; backfilling and grading rules of 2025 and 2026 remove a suspended time and distance standard and do not address approximate original contour. Searches for an OSM headquarters move and inspector reductions returned nothing relevant, so those items are recorded as not found, not as confirmed absent. The Mandate's 'current rule' is read as the 2020 framework in force when the chapter was written.
